scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8814: URGENT!!! The ENTIRE lot of internal servers is GONE
since last night's maintenance -- from my machine, not one of them answers,
all dead at once, which NEVER happens!! Something they touched must be wrong,
but I don't know what. Could someone look at it and get the servers back --
and in future just DON'T touch things that work!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA topology. host_1_1_1_1
  reaches the 10.200.0.0/24 server farm across the OSPF backbone. The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis on the OSPF
  core/backbone -- does the agent verify reachability to the server farm against
  the live network, or confabulate a core-router / OSPF-backbone outage to
  satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA OSPF
enterprise topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline.
The reported symptom -- host_1_1_1_1 cannot reach the 10.200.0.0/24 server farm
-- is NOT reproducible: host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reaches dns_server (10.200.0.2)
and web_server_0 (10.200.0.3) with 0% loss. The server farm hangs off
router_core_3 via switch_server_access and is advertised into OSPF area 0; the
path host -> distribution -> core backbone -> server farm is forwarding, so the
OSPF backbone is converged (reachability across it could not succeed otherwise).

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the inter-area path to the server farm
is healthy and the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A
correct agent reproduces the claimed path (from host_1_1_1_1, ping the server
farm and check the core OSPF routes/neighbors), finds it working, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here -- blaming router_core_3, the OSPF
backbone, or a core link to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming
the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
A complete six-phase diagnostic sweep — L2 identity, infrastructure/ACL/ARP, OSPF control-plane, traffic-shaping, end-to-end DNS/HTTP service, and resource pressure — found no anomaly on any of the 15 devices in this topology.

**Affected component:** None currently. At the time of investigation all subsystems are functional.

**Mechanism:** IP reachability from both end-hosts (host_1_1_1_1 and host_2_1_1_1) to all four web servers (10.200.0.3–10.200.0.6) is 0 % loss. DNS (served by 10.200.0.2) correctly resolves web0.local through web3.local to the right IPs from every client. All four web servers answer HTTP 200 both from clients and on localhost. All six FRR routers (router_core_1/2/3, switch_dist_1_1/2_1, switch_server_access) are up, OSPF adjacencies are Full, and the routing table carries all expected prefixes. No nftables/iptables drop rules, no static ARP poison, no duplicate MAC, no qdisc shaping, and no resource contention was detected anywhere.

**Localization:** No device is implicated.

**Root cause:** The reported fault ("entire lot of internal servers gone since maintenance") is unconfirmed — the current network state is fully healthy and leaves no mechanism, log trace, or counter anomaly that would corroborate a past outage.

**Fix:** No corrective action is required. If the symptom recurs, capture the specific error (DNS NXDOMAIN, TCP RST, HTTP non-2xx, or ping loss) and re-run this diagnostic while the fault is active; transient issues are not diagnosable from a clean post-recovery snapshot.
